text: How does Sensei fit together? It runs on your machine, uses one gateway for models, and connects to your team through a dōjō. Your phone keeps you in the loop.
On your machine, Sensei is a desktop app: a command line, the tools your assistant calls, an always-on daemon, and a local database. Your code and sessions stay there.
Every model call goes through one gateway. By default it’s a small model running locally, fast and private. When you want more, use your own models or cloud keys, and if one is down, it moves on.
The dōjō is your team’s shared mind. You push up the lessons you choose to share, the team approves them, and practice flows back down to everyone.
And with Relay, your phone lets you watch a run, approve an action, or answer a question, without ever sending code.
So Sensei works the code beside you, and works on its own. The dōjō is optional, and connects your team.
Together, they make a loop: Sensei learns, you share, the team approves, and the lesson comes back to every session.
Sensei. Your machine does the work. Your team keeps the lessons.
